articles.title: US Stock Market: Barclays turns hawkish on Fed, sees two rate hikes in 2026
articles.content: Barclays has turned more hawkish on the US Federal Reserve, now expecting two 25-basis-point rate hikes in 2026. The brokerage sees increases in September and December, reversing its earlier call for unchanged rates. The shift follows hawkish remarks from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and renewed concerns over persistent inflation.

articles.title: Jefferies cuts HDFC Bank share price target but retains Buy after CEO opts out of new term. Here’s why

articles.title: Global Market: Chinese property stocks slide as new rules raise consolidation fears
articles.content: Chinese property stocks came under pressure after Beijing introduced new rules aimed at reducing developers’ reliance on homebuyer funds and curbing risks from unfinished projects. While the measures could improve buyer protection, investors fear they may put greater pressure on highly leveraged developers and accelerate industry consolidation.

articles.title: India bonds slump on Fed rate hike bets, benchmark trades at discount
articles.content: Indian government bonds faced a downturn on Monday as yields spiked significantly. Hawkish statements from the head of the U.S. Federal Reserve ignited concerns about imminent rate hikes. Additionally, oil prices surged over ninety dollars a barrel, compounding market pressures. This confluence of events casts a shadow over India's inflation expectations and fiscal health, prompting traders to anticipate local swap rate increases in light of potential Fed actions.

articles.title: Nomura initiates coverage on Clean Max Enviro with Buy call. Check upside potential, key reasons

articles.title: US Stock Market: Warsh signals Fed may need to raise rates if inflation remains elevated
articles.content: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh signalled that the US central bank could raise interest rates if inflation fails to move closer to its 2% target, triggering a sharp shift in market expectations. articles.title: How 90% IPOs in August beat volatile India market to return up to 72% after listing
articles.content: In August, a majority of newly listed IPOs saw a successful debut, outpacing the broader market. Approximately ninety percent of these listings are still trading above their original issue prices, with Tempsens Instruments shining brightly by doubling its value on the first day. Despite the selective nature of the secondary market, the future looks promising with a strong IPO pipeline anticipated to carry through September, enabling substantial fundraising.
